title: Robben Island
summary: Island off Cape Town used from the 17th to 20th centuries as a prison, a hospital for people regarded as socially unacceptable, and a military base. Its maximum-security prison for political prisoners held Nelson Mandela for 18 of his 27 years in jail. The last political prisoners left in 1991, and UNESCO inscribed it in 1999.

uncertainty.note: Span runs from first use as a place of confinement (SAHO) to formal closure of the prison; UNESCO inscription 1999.

where.modern_name: Robben Island, Western Cape, South Africa
where.historical_name: Robben Island, Table Bay (Dutch settlement, later British Cape; later Union and Republic of South Africa)

importance.justification: UNESCO World Heritage Site and the best-known apartheid-era prison, where Nelson Mandela was held.

audience_note: Concerns political imprisonment under apartheid, with discriminatory treatment and punishments of prisoners by colour.

sources.title: Robben Island - UNESCO World Heritage Centre
